summary: Kickoff for Northfield Health onboarding to Redwood. Reviewed goals (pilot + production timeline), security requirements (SSO, SOC2, data residency), deployment choices (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC), initial success metrics and next steps to start a 2-week pilot on dedicated capacity.
transcript:
Header: 2026-09-15 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM); Marta Diaz, Samir Patel, Lena Rogers, Ethan Cole, Rachel Kim (Northfield Health)

Summary: kickoff to align scope and next steps for onboarding. Mentioned security documents and pilot timeline.

00:00:05 Alex Kim: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Alex, I'm the AE working with Northfield, and with me today is Priya our SE and Jordan from customer success. Quick intro from the northfield side?
00:00:20 Marta Diaz: Hi all, Marta here, head of MLOps, I'll be the technical lead for the pilot.
00:00:25 Samir Patel: Samir, CTO, I'll chime in on architecture and timelines.
00:00:30 Lena Rogers: Lena, security - I'll be reviewing SOC2 and SSO requirements.
00:00:35 Alex Kim: Great, thanks. Agenda — high level goals, security/compliance, deployment options (hosted/dedicated/private VPC), success metrics, and decide next steps.
00:01:05 Priya Rao: I'll lead the technical bits, go over our recommended setup and what we'll need from your side.

00:02:10 Priya Rao: Okay start with goals, per Alex you want a pilot to validate latency and cost for your triage assistant and internal knowledge search, is that right Marta?
00:02:18 Marta Diaz: Yes, exactly. Two primary flows: short-turn chat for clinicians (latency sensitive) and bulk embeddings for search (throughput sensitive). We care about P95 latency under 300ms for chat and embeddings throughput throughput of ~2000 requests/hour.
00:02:40 Priya Rao: Great — that maps well to a dedicated pool with autoscale; we can tune batching and KV cache for the embedding pipeline and keep chat on low-latency instances.
00:03:05 Ethan Cole: Quick q on costs — dedicated vs hosted, how big of a delta?
00:03:12 Alex Kim: Short answer: hosted is easiest and often lower for small volume, dedicated gives predictable unit cost at scale. For your volume ranges, dedicated with reserved capacity usually lowers token cost by ~25-40% depending on utilization. We'll put some numbers in the pricing note.

00:04:00 Samir Patel: On data residency — some of our PHI flow will be pseudonymized but we need logs to be retained in-region. Can Redwood guarantee region pinning in a private VPC?
00:04:12 Priya Rao: Yes — for Private deployments we support region pinning and you can run the control plane in your VPC or in a customer-managed network. For Dedicated we offer region selection per pool, and we can enable in-region retention for logs.
00:04:38 Lena Rogers: Are audit logs RFC compliant? And KMS options?
00:04:45 Priya Rao: We support customer-managed KMS and HSM for key separation, and audit logs are available with configurable retention. We'll share the SOC2 and infra diagrams in the security pack.

00:05:30 Alex Kim: Noted - we'll share SOC2 + security pack after the call. Link placeholder: https://redwood.ai/security-pack/northfield (we'll send actual link).

00:06:00 Priya Rao: Technical checklist — we typically need: access to a test dataset (sanitized), network egress rules, SSO/SAML metadata for SSO setup, and expected QPS and sample prompts so we can repro latency.
00:06:22 Marta Diaz: We can provide sample prompts and a scrubbed dataset. For SSO we use Okta — we'll share metadata.

00:07:10 Ethan Cole: For VPC peering, do you require a static IP or do you support dynamic egress?
00:07:16 Priya Rao: For peering we prefer static routes; in many cases customers use a NAT gateway, but we'll capture the exact network diagram in the SE deep dive.

00:08:05 Rachel Kim: Timeline — We want pilot started by end of September and production by mid-November. Is that realistic?
00:08:12 Alex Kim: That is possible. Typical timeline: 2-week pilot, then iterated onboarding for production which can take 4-6 weeks depending on integration. So mid-November is doable if pilot starts 9/29 and we get sign-off quickly.

00:09:00 Priya Rao: For the pilot we recommend a small dedicated pool, with the chat route pinned to low-latency instances and embeddings routed to a higher throughput quantized variant. We'll supply model version recommendations based on your latency/cost target.
00:09:25 Marta Diaz: Are these model variants open-source or Redwood's hosted ensembles?
00:09:30 Priya Rao: We provide curated open models and Redwood-verified profiles; you can use open models, or we can help pick a variant. If you need on-prem/private we can discuss model licensing separately.

00:10:10 Lena Rogers: Encryption at rest and in transit?
00:10:14 Priya Rao: TLS in transit, and encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated. For hosted API we have KMS integration options.

00:11:00 Samir Patel: Any benchmarking we can run early? We'd like to run some perf tests against our sample prompts.
00:11:07 Priya Rao: Yes — we'll provide a benchmarking harness and a spreadsheet for you to populate. We can also run an initial baseline in our staging infra. Note — transcription sometimes misreports KV cache as K-V cash ha, but we mean KV cache for inference speedups.

00:12:15 Alex Kim: Competitors question — Marta asked if we evaluated Anthropic and OpenAI previously. Marta, do you want to talk about that?
00:12:23 Marta Diaz: We ran POCs with both. Anthropic had good safety features, OpenAI strong models but cost and network constraints were an issue. We're interested in predictable serving economics — that's why Redwood's dedicated option appeals.

00:13:30 Priya Rao: On observability — Redwood Console provides token-level cost, latency per route, and rollout controls for model versioning. We'll show dashboards in the SE deep dive.

00:14:12 Ethan Cole: Any SSO pitfalls? Last time we had SAML attributes mapping issues with another vendor.
00:14:20 Jordan Lee: Jordan from CSM — we typically create a test SP in Okta and map attributes in advance; we'll work with your IdP admin to reduce friction.

00:15:30 Marta Diaz: Questions about retention — can we turn off retention for certain logs in staging?
00:15:36 Priya Rao: Yes, configurable retention per environment. For compliance we can default to stricter settings in prod.

00:16:40 Samir Patel: On the cost model — reservation commitments? We might be open to a monthly commit for a predictable price.
00:16:47 Alex Kim: We offer reserved capacity contracts for Dedicated with monthly/annual commits. We'll send a pricing sketch post-call.

00:18:05 Priya Rao: Integration checklist items — 1) network diagram, 2) SSO metadata, 3) sample prompts/dataset, 4) list of routes and success metrics (latency targets), 5) compliance contacts.
00:18:25 Marta Diaz: We'll share the network diagram and sample prompts by end of next week.

00:19:40 Alex Kim: Any blockers from security, Lena?
00:19:45 Lena Rogers: We'll need to review SOC2 and vendor risk questionnaire. Also we need confirmation on KMS and audit log retention options. If those are okay we'll move forward.
00:20:05 Alex Kim: We'll send the security pack with specifics and a vendor questionnaire response.

00:21:30 Priya Rao: Ops question — does Northfield have a preferred CI flow for model rollouts?
00:21:38 Rachel Kim: We'll probably use GitOps for infra and a canary process for model rollouts.
00:21:45 Priya Rao: Perfect — Redwood supports canary rollouts, automatic fallback policies, and route-based rollouts. We'll document that in the runbook.

00:23:00 Alex Kim: Ok let's talk pilot scope — two routes: clinician chat (latency target 300ms P95) and embeddings indexing (throughput 2000 reqs/hr). Pilot duration two weeks, target start 2026-09-29.
00:23:20 Marta Diaz: Agreed. Success criteria: P95 latency under 300ms for chat, embedding throughput sustained at target and cost within expected range, and no critical security findings.

00:24:10 Priya Rao: I'll put together the exact instance types and expected cost ranges for the pilot and share a config template.

00:25:00 Samir Patel: For networking, would we prefer Private deployment or Dedicated in our VPC? Which path is faster?
00:25:08 Priya Rao: Dedicated in Redwood-managed infra is the fastest path — you get reserved capacity without full private control plane. Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) take longer due to more setup and governance. For your timeline I'd recommend Dedicated for the pilot, then evaluate Private if needed for prod.

00:26:15 Ethan Cole: Any sample runbooks or onboarding playbooks?
00:26:22 Jordan Lee: Yes — we'll share the onboarding playbook and runbook after this call.

00:27:40 Marta Diaz: One last question on telemetry: can we stream logs to our SIEM?
00:27:46 Priya Rao: Yes, we support log forwarding to external sinks and can integrate with your SIEM via secure forwarding.

00:28:30 Alex Kim: Alright let's recap. Next steps: Alex sends onboarding playbook and SOC2/security pack; Priya schedules SE deep dive (VPC, networking) next week; Marta provides sample prompts and network diagram; Lena provides security contact. Pilot target start 2026-09-29.
00:29:10 Marta Diaz: Sounds good.
00:29:20 Samir Patel: Thanks everyone.
00:29:25 Alex Kim: Thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.

00:30:00 [End of recorded portion — side conversation about internal scheduling omitted]

Notes: Transcript has occasional mishears (e.g., "K-V cash" instead of KV cache), speaker labels are mostly accurate. References: onboarding playbook (link will be sent), security pack link placeholder.

Action items (captured above): Alex to send playbook and security docs; Priya to schedule SE deep dive; Customer to provide prompts/network diagram; CSM to track timeline.

End of transcript.
